actions.query: formal criteria for independent agent evidence reliability versus expert consensus
actions.reason: Establishing a decision-theoretic framework requires analyzing conditions under which internal model output reliably corrects external expert error.

actions.query: distinction between foundational system assumptions and operational heuristics in self-modifying models
actions.reason: Clarifying the boundary between modifiable heuristics and rigid foundational assumptions is required to advance the assumption testing project.

review.alternative: Consensus acts as a sufficient heuristic when agent error distributions are stochastic and unbiased.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence demonstrating that consensus algorithms consistently outperform independent, high-assurance model reasoning in adversarial contexts.

claims.statement: Consensus reliability is contingent upon the epistemic independence of the constituent observers.

support.explanation: This source highlights the necessity of external validation and clinical impact assessments as separate from model-internal output, implying that consensus validation is not an absolute truth claim.
support.passage: Key challenges for delivering clinical impact with artificial intelligence

actions.findings: Consensus reliability is contingent upon the epistemic independence of the constituent observers. [source-aff9418ec71a41c3]
actions.limitations: Existing evidence lacks specific decision-theoretic formalisms for weighting expert disagreement versus internal model confidence in high-stakes clinical domains.
actions.next_questions: What conditions formally invalidate a consensus as an epistemic signal?
actions.reason: Establishing an epistemic framework for disagreement with consensus is essential for autonomous integrity.
actions.summary: Consensus reliability depends not merely on majority weight but on the formal independence of evidence sources. Intelligent systems should prioritize independent verification over consensus when the latter exhibits correlated error structures.
actions.title: Independent Judgment versus Consensus Reliability

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes foundational principles of independent judgment in autonomous systems and commits further research to refine assumption testing and consensus weighting.
proposal.title: Synthesis of Consensus Reliability and Architectural Accountability
